stories.title: Supreme Court ruling on Quebec's secularism law expected Friday morning
stories.summary: The case stems from a Quebec law known as Bill 21, which bans public servants in positions of authority from wearing religious symbols while on the job.
stories.detail: On Friday morning, a record number of journalists and lawyers of record who've been sworn to confidentiality will be the first to read a historic judgment from the Supreme Court of Canada determining the fate of Quebec's controversial Bill 21.

details.summary: The case stems from a Quebec law known as Bill 21, which bans public servants in positions of authority from wearing religious symbols while on the job.

On Friday morning, a record number of journalists and lawyers of record who've been sworn to confidentiality will be the first to read a historic judgment from the Supreme Court of Canada determining the fate of Quebec's controversial Bill 21.
The Supreme Court is set to rule on Quebec’s secularism law in a landmark case that could reshape how governments use the notwithstanding clause.

stories.title: Doug Ford advises Ontarians to protect against home invasions by any means
stories.summary: Doug Ford said Thursday he wants to see legal changes to address a spate of home invasions, and in the meantime he advised people to protect their families by any means necessary.

details.summary: Doug Ford said Thursday he wants to see legal changes to address a spate of home invasions, and in the meantime he advised people to protect their families by any means necessary.

The premier says he owns a gun and would not hesitate to use it on someone trying to break into his home, advising people without guns to use knives or baseball bats to protect themselves and their children.

stories.title: Trump alleges ‘fake’ economic figures released before US midterms but doesn’t provide evidence
stories.summary: President says it was a deliberate decision to release 'fake' growth numbers before US midterm elections.
stories.detail: In a Thanksgiving post, the US president seeks investigation after blue wave of Democrats unseat Republicans Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party. In a holiday message on social media tinged with bitterness, the US president wished a happy thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”.

details.summary: President says it was a deliberate decision to release 'fake' growth numbers before US midterm elections.
